sketches.title: Career Cosmic Roast
sketches.premise: You get the same ordinary job title as your rival, then write its horoscope: a tiny prophecy about what will happen at work today. Keep the job recognizable, but make the stars dramatically overconfident; the host awards points for how far your prediction goes without losing the job’s core duty.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the prophecy still predicts something a person doing that job could plausibly experience while clearly preserving the title’s main job.
sketches.move_shape: Write one sentence of horoscope in up to 160 characters, naming the job and predicting its workday; for **baker**: “Today, your dough rises beautifully, but a jealous wedding cake demands a corner office.”

sketches.title: Office Omen
sketches.premise: The host deals a plain job title and asks both players for one ominous sign from its workday. Make the sign strange, specific, and just believable enough that a tired worker might nod instead of calling security.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the omen is a sign or warning tied to a real task, tool, or setting of the dealt job.
sketches.move_shape: Write one sentence describing the job’s bad sign, with invented details allowed; for **dentist**: “When the patient’s toothache whispers your name, cancel lunch and inspect the X-ray twice.”

sketches.title: Promotion Prophecy
sketches.premise: Both players horoscope a job title by predicting the ridiculous path to its next promotion. The title must remain the engine of the prophecy; otherwise you have simply written fan fiction about a person with a clipboard.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the prediction concerns advancement earned through or caused by the dealt job’s actual work.
sketches.move_shape: Write one sentence predicting how this worker gets promoted; for **librarian**: “Return every book on time, and the mayor will promote you to Keeper of the City’s Forbidden Shelf.”

sketches.title: Shift Signs
sketches.premise: A job title becomes a horoscope sign with a lucky event and a warning for the next shift. Both players answer the same title, and the host rewards the entry that squeezes the most drama from two ordinary pieces of work.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that both the lucky event and warning stay connected to two recognizable nouns belonging to the job.
sketches.move_shape: Write one sentence containing a lucky sign and a warning, each tied to a job noun; for **bus driver**: “A green light blesses your route, but the ticket machine begins judging every passenger.”

sketches.title: Starry Shift Report
sketches.premise: Write the horoscope a job title would receive from a brutally cheerful career astrologer. Include what goes well and what goes wrong, then let the host score how boldly you transform the shift without quietly changing the profession.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the good and bad predictions both happen during recognizable duties of the dealt job.
sketches.move_shape: Write one sentence with a success and a setback in the same shift; for **cook**: “Your soup wins the stars’ blessing, while one runaway pea starts a diplomatic crisis.”

sketches.title: Zodiac on the Job
sketches.premise: The host deals a boring job title and two everyday nouns linked to it. Turn them into a horoscope that predicts one absurd consequence, while keeping both nouns in play; the host’s commentary gets sharper when your fate sounds suspiciously deserved.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the prediction uses both dealt nouns as recognizable parts of the job’s work, without revealing the card’s hidden truth.
sketches.move_shape: Write one sentence using both nouns in a job horoscope; for **mail carrier — letter, door**: “A letter opens the door to glory, but the door opens first and asks why you are late.”
